parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no facility bans, no custody-placement rule, no documented police sweeps or trans-targeted violence — so it sits well above the universal-exposure tier (0.45 and below). But there is similarly no documented positive: no legal gender recognition, no document-mismatch procedure for a visitor whose passport diverges from presentation, no gender-identity ground in the employment or hate-crime provisions, and an explicitly thin, encyclopaedic record. The 2016 LGBT-wide poll and generic 'stigmatisation' language describe an unfriendly-but-not-hostile climate and are not trans-specific or current, so I weight them lightly. Document checks at borders and hotels are the real friction point, but with no documented refusal, detention or harassment the outcome is an open question, not a known exposure. Comparing to the anchors, the absence of any documented acceptance or working remedy keeps it out of the 0.65 tier; the absence of any documented recurring visitor-facing harm keeps it above 0.45.
